item.text: {"summary":"A shrub native to Southwest China, specifically Guizhou, Hubei and Sichuan, the China rose grows in hedges or thickets. Its wild form has five pink-to-red petals and red hips, while its purplish-brown branches may bear many curved spines or none.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Young plant parts, flower buds and flowers are brewed or eaten; rosehip flesh is eaten raw or cooked, and ground seeds are added to foods.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p9"]}}
